arxiv-2107-04553.title: Can Deep Neural Networks Predict Data Correlations from Column Names?
arxiv-2107-04553.creator: Immanuel Trummer
arxiv-2107-04553.description: Abstract . Recent publications suggest using natural language analysis on database schema elements to guide tuning and profiling efforts. The underlying hypothesis is that state-of-the-art language processing methods, so-called language models, are able to extract information on data properties from schema text.

arxiv-2307-13928.title: Beyond Strict Competition: Approximate Convergence of Multi Agent Q-Learning Dynamics
arxiv-2307-13928.creator: Aamal Abbas Hussain, Francesco Belardinelli, Georgios Piliouras
arxiv-2307-13928.description: Abstract The behaviour of multi-agent learning in competitive settings is often considered under the restrictive assumption of a zero-sum game. Only under this strict requirement is the behaviour of learning well understood; beyond this, learning dynamics can often display non-convergent behaviours which prevent fixed-point analysis. Nonetheless, many relevant competitive games do not satisfy the zero-sum assumption.

arxiv-2401-10991.title: Dust around massive stars is agnostic to galactic environment: New insights from PHAT/BEAST Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2401-10991.creator: Christina Willecke Lindberg, Claire E. Murray, Julianne J. Dalcanton, J. E. G. Peek, Karl D. Gordon
arxiv-2401-10991.description: Abstract Resolving the environments of massive stars is crucial for understanding their formation mechanisms and their impact on galaxy evolution. An important open question is whether massive stars found in diffuse regions outside spiral arms formed in-situ or migrated there after forming in denser environments.

arxiv-2411-11696.title: Active droplets controlled by enzymatic reactions
arxiv-2411-11696.creator: Jacques Fries 1 , Javier Díaz 2 , Marie Jardat 1 , Ignacio Pagonabarraga 2 , Pierre Illien 1 , Vincent Dahirel 1
arxiv-2411-11696.description: Abstract The formation of condensates is now considered as a major organization principle of eukaryotic cells. Several studies have recently shown that the properties of these condensates are affected by enzymatic reactions. We propose here a simple generic model to study the interplay between two enzyme populations and a two-state protein.

arxiv-2412-16892.title: An Interaction Design Toolkit for Physical Task Guidance with Artificial Intelligence and Mixed Reality
arxiv-2412-16892.creator: Arthur Caetano, Alejandro Aponte, Misha Sra
arxiv-2412-16892.description: Abstract . Physical skill acquisition, from sports techniques to surgical procedures, requires instruction and feedback. In the absence of a human expert, Physical Task Guidance (PTG) systems can offer a promising alternative. These systems integrate Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Mixed Reality (MR) to provide realtime feedback and guidance as users practice and learn skills using physical tools and objects.

pmc-10736762.title: THE MODERATING ROLE OF POSITIVE SOLITUDE IN THE RELATIONS BETWEEN LONELINESS AND DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS
pmc-10736762.creator: Dikla Segel-Karpas, Yuval Palgi, Sharon Ost Mor, Yaira Hamama Raz, Mayan Shacham, Menachem Ben-Ezra, Lee Greenblatt Kimron
pmc-10736762.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Positive solitude, the choice of being alone to engage in meaningful inner or physical, spiritual, mental, or cognitive activity/ experience, was recently suggested as a stand-alone phenomenon differentiated from loneliness and negative solitude. As loneliness was previously found to have adverse implications for mental health, the present study examined whether the ability to engage in positive solitude can moderate the harmful effect of loneliness on depressive symptoms. The sample consisted of 520 community dwelling older adults in Israel aged 68-87 (Mage=72.66).

pmc-11496535.description: During aging, changes in body composition can result in sarcopenic obesity, which is a condition in which obesity occurs accompanied by the loss of muscle mass and strength caused by sarcopenia.
